QUESTION OF THE WEEK - Economists were asked for their forecasts of first quarter 1997 consumer price index (CPI) inflation and underlying inflation.
Economists are optimistic on the outlook for inflation, and said that even the biggest threat, wages growth, should remain under control in 1997.

With the effects of last year's three official rate cuts and the competition induced round of cuts earlier this year still feeding through, the CPI is seen remaining low in the March quarter, with some expecting a negative result.
A rise in line with median forecasts would see the annual rate down to 1.2-1.3 percent.

The underlying rate is seen matching its December quarter rise, which would keep the annual rate constant at 2.1 percent. With wages seen under control, and little pressures seen in manufacturing and import price indexes, underlying inflation looks comfortably ensconced in the lower end of the RBA's two to three percent target range.

LABOUR FORCE -- While a rise is universally expected after the weakness on the February data, economists said the picture was still of insufficient employment growth to unable to make inroads into the unemployment rate. However, expectations are that employment should strengthen through the year, with upturns in the retail and housing sectors leading to increased jobs. The outlook for employment has also been helped by signs of resilience in the job vacancies and overtime data, as well as some signs of recovery in the ANZ job advertisement series.
